title: Large serine recombinase-mediated gene insertion for high-throughput screens: advantages; design principles; and applications.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Retrieved the open-access full text (112,185 characters) and its data availability statement, which reads verbatim 'No new data was generated in this article.' Downloaded and listed the Europe PMC supplementary package (0.67 MB): all 14 files are figure images (.gif/.webp), no tables or data files. Searched the whole text for GitHub, Zenodo, Figshare, Dryad, Addgene links and for GEO/SRA/BioProject accessions: zero hits. Europe PMC text-mining returned only two preprint DOIs (citations), and NCBI link queries returned only the PMC record itself.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That Tables 1 and 2 are qualitative method-comparison tables (targeted-integration strategies; large serine recombinase metrics versus programmable nucleases and transposases) rather than measurement tables - I read their in-text context but the tables themselves are embedded in the article body, not downloadable files.

a1_downloadable.note: There is no dataset. The data availability statement says 'No new data was generated in this article.' The only downloadable attachments are the six article figures as images. Nothing to download, so A1 fails and scoring stops here.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No table exists, so no label column exists. Any outcome (for example integration efficiency of a recombinase) would have to be assembled from the ~150 primary papers this review cites, each with its own assay and units.

a3_inputs_present.note: No sequences, no recognition-site sequences, no accessions in any machine-readable form; the review refers to enzymes by name in prose.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable - no measurement table. Efficiency figures quoted in the prose come from different labs using different readouts (flow cytometry, amplicon sequencing, colony counts).

a5_enough_rows.note: Zero data rows attached to this paper. The two in-text tables are qualitative comparisons of methods, on the order of a handful of rows each.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits, but only because there is nothing there.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No counts to compare - the paper reports no dataset size and the supplement contains no tables.

a8_label_provenance.note: No labels. Efficiency numbers discussed in the text are second-hand values quoted from other publications, which would make any assembled label a mixture of assays and reporting conventions rather than one measurement.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: this is a narrative review that generated no data, so there is nothing to train on or test against.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a recombinase enzyme's protein sequence to predict how efficiently it inserts DNA at its target site.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would need one row per large serine recombinase (an enzyme that stitches a DNA payload into a chromosome at a short recognition site), with its protein sequence and the measured insertion efficiency. This paper supplies zero such rows.
plain_idea.predict: Insertion efficiency, normally measured by counting how many cells gained a fluorescent or drug-resistance marker, or by sequencing across the new DNA junction. This review only quotes such numbers from other papers, in prose.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups building 'landing pad' cell lines for large-scale variant testing pick a recombinase largely by habit; a predictor would let them pick one for a new target site. But that project needs the measurement tables from the primary papers, not this review.

ml_idea: None available from this paper. The underlying idea worth chasing - predicting large serine recombinase activity and target-site preference from enzyme sequence - would have to start from the primary datasets this review cites, for example the genome-mining study that characterised thousands of candidate recombinases and measured integration efficiency for a subset, not from the review itself.

effort.compute_note: Only the 0.67 MB figure-image supplement exists; no modelling workload to estimate.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement - it says 'No new data was generated in this article.' That took one request and kills the candidate.

verdict_reason: Narrative review with an explicit 'no new data' statement; the only downloadable files are figure images, so A1, A2, A3, A5 and A8 all fail. If the recombinase-prediction angle is wanted, screen the primary papers it cites (the large-scale recombinase genome-mining and landing-pad screening studies) instead.
